root_cause: The 100-million-distinct-k-mer fallback doubles the pass count and partitions by minimizer ID. A minimizer with 135,288,763 distinct k-mers cannot be split by that operation, so it repeatedly exceeds the same limit. A failed later pass also retries already emitted data, reopens and truncates its output while the old writer remains open, and increments index counters again.
minimal_fix: Remove the hard-coded cutoff and recursive retry from merge_super_buckets_mem; finish each requested partition once with the existing graph, profile, and serialization algorithms.
memory_tradeoff: The removed cutoff was a k-mer cardinality heuristic, not a RAM budget. Memory now follows the size of each loaded super-bucket; the real oversized bucket used 12.4946 GiB in this isolated replay. No bounded-memory fallback was added.
